title: Action Beats & Rainbow Words
objective: Listen, act and connect letters with familiar words.

chapters.title: Clap your hands.
chapters.objective: Listen to an action word and say clap

chapters.title: I know my alphabet.
chapters.objective: Recognize an English letter by listening

chapters.title: Let us read.
chapters.objective: Blend familiar letters to make a short word

chapters.title: Fun with Special Letters
chapters.objective: Identify vowels a, e, i, o, u in simple words

chapters.title: The Rainbow
chapters.objective: Identify and describe an illustrated colour

activities.prompt: Clap two times. Now say clap with Miss Julie.

evidence.description: Learner attempts the action word after modeling.

teaching.teacherQuestion: Miss Julie claps two times. Listen: clap. Now say clap!

hints.en: Clap means bringing your hands together.
hints.hi: Clap मतलब ताली बजाना। अब कहो clap.
hints.mr: Clap म्हणजे टाळी वाजवणे. आता clap म्हण.

teaching.expectedEvidence: Child attempts the English word clap, with no demand to clap physically.

activities.prompt: Listen to the letter B. Find B from A, B and D.

evidence.description: Learner distinguishes the named letter from distractors.

teaching.teacherQuestion: Look at A, B and D. Listen closely. Point to B.

hints.en: B is one letter of the English alphabet.
hints.hi: यह letter B है। सुनो और B चुनो.
hints.mr: हे B अक्षर आहे. ऐक आणि B निवड.

teaching.retryEnglish: Listen to B. Try saying B.
teaching.expectedEvidence: Child identifies the heard letter B from mixed positions.

activities.prompt: Put c, a and t together. What word did we make?

evidence.description: Learner builds cat and attempts to say it.

teaching.teacherQuestion: We have c, a and t. Say the word with me: cat.

hints.en: We can join c, a and t to make cat.
hints.hi: C, A, T साथ में cat बनता है।
hints.mr: C, A, T मिळून cat हा शब्द होतो.

teaching.retryEnglish: Listen: c, a, t. Together: cat.
teaching.expectedEvidence: Child sequences c a t or says cat after a model; do not score unassisted literacy before review.

activities.prompt: Listen: a, e, i, o, u are vowels. Find the vowel a in cat.

evidence.description: Learner identifies a vowel in a familiar word; written missing-vowel work remains teacher-led.

teaching.teacherQuestion: A, E, I, O and U are vowels. Look at cat. Find the vowel a.
modelLines: The vowel a is in cat.

hints.en: The five vowel letters are a, e, i, o and u.
hints.hi: A, E, I, O, U vowels हैं। Cat में a चुनो।
hints.mr: A, E, I, O, U हे स्वर आहेत. Cat मध्ये a निवड.

teaching.retryEnglish: Find the letter a in cat.
teaching.expectedEvidence: Child identifies a in cat; adult-led written missing-vowel exercises remain required.

activities.prompt: Look at three colour cards. Which one is red?

evidence.description: Learner selects or names a presented colour.

teaching.teacherQuestion: Our rainbow picture has red and blue. Point to red.

hints.en: Red is a colour of the rainbow.
hints.hi: Red मतलब लाल। उस कार्ड को चुनो.
hints.mr: Red म्हणजे लाल. ते कार्ड निवड.

teaching.retryEnglish: Look at the red card. Say red.
teaching.expectedEvidence: Child identifies red against a colour and shape distractor.

activities.prompt: Miss Julie claps once. Can you say clap without me?

evidence.description: Independent spoken English attempt at clap, with a model on request.

activities.prompt: Listen for B. Find B after the letters move to new places.

evidence.description: Locates B in a new randomized visible order.

activities.prompt: Miss Julie points to an original cat picture. Say: I see a cat.

evidence.description: An English word or short model phrase about the pictured cat; no accent score.

activities.prompt: Listen: a is a vowel. Find a in cat, then try finding e in pen.

evidence.description: Identifies a and e as vowels in two new authored word cards.

activities.prompt: Miss Julie holds a red colour card. Say: It is red.

evidence.description: Attempts red or the supported short sentence in English.

activities.prompt: Tiny homework: Find one colour around you later and say its English name.

evidence.description: Receives short spoken offline homework; no family recording, upload or XP grant.

activities.prompt: Let us practise counting to five with gentle actions. Listen, then say one action word with me.

evidence.description: Teacher observes the five-count action sequence or accessible alternatives, not just microphone speech.

activities.prompt: Try a different movement in our own action game. Can you say wave, sing, touch or blink?

evidence.description: Teacher checks the complete set of action substitutions and safe access needs.

activities.prompt: Listen: knee. Find the knee picture. We will also learn bend, floor, turn and the other action words.

evidence.description: Teacher checks every target vocabulary item from the printed activity, not this sample word alone.

activities.prompt: Look at a big letter and its small partner. Find them together; trace them with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher checks all 26 uppercase/lowercase pairings and actual tracing work.

activities.prompt: Imagine two letter cards looking for partners. Say a letter as your teacher helps you match it.

evidence.description: Teacher observes physical letter-card matching or an accessible alternative.

activities.prompt: Listen for the middle sound e in pen. Choose the matching picture as your teacher checks the path.

evidence.description: Teacher verifies each word choice along the full middle-e picture maze.

activities.prompt: Hear short words like am, be, in and up. Read and write the full two-letter set with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher checks all assigned two-letter groups and notebook writing.

activities.prompt: Try making a word from the an family. Next practise en, in, op and un in your notebook.

evidence.description: Teacher verifies each word family and written examples, not just the initial word.

activities.prompt: Study the picture and choose the sound that completes its word; write the letters with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher confirms all picture-letter choices and legible completed written words.

activities.prompt: Listen: sun, Sunday. Which little word begins the longer word? Try the other pairs too.

evidence.description: Teacher checks man/mango, pen/pencil, win/window, pop/popcorn and sun/Sunday.

activities.prompt: Listen to the five vowel letters: a, e, i, o, u. Say them slowly with Miss Julie.

evidence.description: Teacher confirms the vowel-versus-consonant distinction; no accent scoring.

activities.prompt: Find the vowel in ball, then practise with dog, cup, ice, tree, onion, zebra and umbrella.

evidence.description: Teacher checks vowel identification across all eight pictured word examples.

activities.prompt: A letter is missing in s_n. Which vowel belongs there? Complete the remaining words on paper.

evidence.description: Teacher checks written missing vowels in sun, cat, fish, egg and owl.

activities.prompt: What colours do you notice in our original rainbow? Share a question, then sing with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher observes discussion and the textbook poem separately using permitted classroom materials.

activities.prompt: Find violet on the rainbow. Now locate all seven colours, including indigo.

evidence.description: Teacher verifies recognition of all seven colour words.

activities.prompt: Listen to the word sky. Say it, then write the full dictation list with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher checks rainbow, sky, peeping, clouds, orange and indigo in a notebook.

activities.prompt: Look at an original sky picture. Complete a short phrase with a word from the picture.

evidence.description: Teacher checks both printed phrases and corresponding written answers.

activities.prompt: Listen: an apple, a cat and the sun. Notice how we choose a, an or the.

evidence.description: Teacher checks all printed article examples and explains introductory sound-based usage.

activities.prompt: Choose a, an or the for a practice picture. Complete the remaining workbook blanks with your teacher.

evidence.description: Teacher signs off all twelve article blanks on printed page 9; one speaking answer is not enough.
